Subject: Region fit evaluation — hosting pathways & data residency follow-up

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on EuroBank's requirements and constraints: 

What we heard (high level):
- EU production data must remain in-region for customer-facing inference (transactional PII flows).
- APAC product teams are evaluating a pilot but currently require APAC data residency and lower latency than a cross-region hop can provide.
- Procurement/security will need SOC2 evidence, and the legal team will want clear routing/fallback rules in the contract.

Options we discussed (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted (Redwood API) pinned to EU region — fastest to ship, our EU hosting keeps data at-rest and in-region; works for most EU-only workloads.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) in a cloud region — predictable throughput and potential to colocate in EU or APAC; good middle ground for larger pipelines.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — required when APAC residency + full network isolation/policy control is non-negotiable.

Open questions for you:
- Is the APAC requirement blocking for your Q2 pilot, or can the pilot run in EU while APAC plans a later Private/Dedicated rollout?
- Any hard latency SLOs we should target (p95 in ms) for retail checkout flows?

Proposed next steps:
- Ben: prepare a short matrix (EU hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with latency/cost/lead time (will attach).
- Monica: outline procurement evidence pack and timeline for SOC2 + KMS integration.
- Elena / EuroBank: confirm whether pilot can be EU-only for Q2 or if APAC must be ready in parallel.

I've attached a draft comparison table and an EU perf matrix Ben will flesh out. If that plan sounds good I'll lock in a technical follow-up next week (30–45 min) with your infra lead.

Thanks — Sean

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear summary. A couple of clarifications from my side: 

1) APAC requirement: for our merchant checkout pilot APAC is currently blocking — we need APAC-resident inference for any flow that touches local cardholder data. We can consider a separate pilot that is EU-only, but leadership prefers a plan that includes an APAC path.

2) Latency: target p95 < 300ms for async scoring and < 120ms p95 for real-time fraud decisions at peak. If cross-region routing will push real-time above that, it won't be acceptable for checkout.

3) Fallbacks: in cases of EU region outage, what does Redwood recommend for failover? We need a written fallback policy (e.g., local retry, route to dedicated pool, degrade to cached decision) to include in our SOW.

Please share the matrix and the fallback policy doc; we'll review with infra and legal. Also looping in our infra lead (cc'd in a separate note) for one technical follow-up.

Best,
Elena

Elena — quick technical note from our side based on your latency targets and residency needs. TL;DR: EU-hosted satisfies EU residency and will meet the <120ms p95 for many EU geographies; APAC residency will require either Dedicated or Private VPC deployed in APAC to hit your latency numbers. Details: 

- Hosted (EU pinned): Data stays in-region at rest and in transit; we provide KV/prefix caching to reduce token latency; typical p95 for EU customers (major metros) is ~80–150ms for short prompt generations and <100ms for small scoring calls.
- Cross-region routing (EU -> APAC): introduces 120–250ms additional RTT depending on origin; not acceptable for your <120ms p95 real-time SLO.
- Dedicated (APAC region): reserved GPU pools can be spun up in APAC; lead time ~4–6 weeks with capacity commit. Good option if you want Redwood-managed infra but local residency.
- Private VPC: full network isolation, KMS/HSM integration, and on-prem options; longer lead time (6–10+ weeks) depending on customer infra readiness.

Fallbacks: we recommend a layered fallback policy for SOW: 1) automatic retry to same region with exponential backoff, 2) failover to dedicated APAC pool (if configured), 3) serve a cached verdict with explicit degrade-mode scoring model, 4) alert + circuit-break to block risky flows. We'll draft a formal fallback appendix for legal.

I'm attaching a short perf/cost matrix (first pass). Happy to review live in the technical follow-up.

— Ben

- For Dedicated/Private: procurement will also require network topology, KMS/HSM integration plan, and a runbook for on-call/support escalation. Procurement lead time: expect 6–10 weeks.
